question: A safety officer wants the total energy figure, in kilojoules, for 3 identical sleds, each expressed in kilojoules. Each sled's figure is its energy of motion plus 20 J from a push. Each sled has a mass of 58 kg. Its speed, in m/s, is found by doubling the sum of 7 and 3 and then subtracting 9. What is the total energy figure, in kJ?

A 15 000 g cart moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 1·x³ - 1·x² is itself changing at x = 4. Its energy of motion is expressed in kilojoules. A battery adds 22 kJ to the cart's energy account, the total is multiplied by 5 for 5 identical carts, and a heater adds 6 kJ. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?

A lab wants the total energy figure, in kilojoules, for 2 identical carts. Each cart's figure is its energy of motion, expressed in kilojoules, plus 23 kJ from a heater, plus 20 kJ from a battery. Each cart has a mass of 29 kg. Its speed, in m/s, equals the number of ways to choose 4 sensors from 7. What is the total energy figure, in kJ?

A club wants the net energy balance, in kilojoules, of a launcher's battery: 30 kJ drawn by the launcher's heater is subtracted from the net delivered energy, expressed in kilojoules. The net delivered energy is the combined energy of motion of 6 identical 5 000 g projectiles, less 15 J lost to friction. Each projectile's speed, in m/s, is the greatest common divisor of 129 and 368. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?

A depot wants the rated force, in kilonewtons: a 16 kN reserve is added after 21 kN supplied by a gravity assist is subtracted from the force for 7 identical 163 000 g carts, expressed in kilonewtons. The carts are 2.2 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 3x³ - 5x² is itself changing at x = 3. What is the rated force, in kN?

A coach wants the total energy figure, in joules, of 8 identical sleds plus 4 J stored in a starting gate. Each sled's figure is its energy of motion plus 23 J from a push plus 2 J from a nudge. Each sled has a mass of 39 000 g. Its speed, in m/s, is the larger root of x² - 7x + 10 = 0. What is the total energy figure, in J?

A depot wants the total force, in kilonewtons, for 7 sites, each with 10 identical carts, with each cart's force stated in kilonewtons. Each cart's force is what accelerates its 48 000 g mass plus 29 N of friction. The carts are 1.6 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the number of ways to choose 4 wheels from 7. What is the total force, in kN?

A depot wants the force, in kilonewtons, to accelerate a 38 kg cart. The acceleration, in m/s², is found by taking the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 7x from x = 0 to x = 1, multiplying by 3, adding 22, and subtracting 15. The cart runs on a 10 m rail. What is the force, in kN?

A depot wants the total force, in newtons, for 6 identical lines. Each line's figure is the force for 9 identical 172 kg carts, less 13 N recovered by a regenerative unit, less 7 N supplied by a slope. The carts are 2 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², is the greatest common divisor of 261 and 17. What is the total force, in N?

A coach wants the total energy of motion, in joules, of 9 identical sleds, each having gained 17 J from a push after losing 14 J to friction. Each sled has a mass of 14 kg and is 1.1 m long. Its speed, in m/s, equals the number of ways to choose 2 runners from 10. What is the total energy of motion, in J?

A dock wants the net force, in kilonewtons, for 2 identical 107 kg carts, less 9 N supplied by a slope. The carts' acceleration, in m/s², is found by multiplying the sum of 9 and 6 by 3 and subtracting 15. The carts share one winch. What is the net force, in kN?

A technician on a lab bench is tallying the total energy delivered to a test rig, and the very last entry she adds to the tally is a fixed 26 J contributed by a pre-loaded spring. Just before that entry, she had multiplied a running total by 12, because the rig fires 12 identical cycles. That running total was itself 6 times the energy of motion of a single sliding cart, since the rig carries 6 such carts. Each cart has a mass of 27 kg and slides at a speed in metres per second equal to the largest whole number that divides both 363 and 346 without remainder. What is the final energy in the tally, in J?

The net force a tugboat crew finally logs is 4 N less than an intermediate reading taken during the trial. That intermediate reading was 5 N more than the combined push of 10 identical thrusters acting together. Each thruster on its own accelerates a test block of mass 37,000 g at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller of the two values of x for which x² - 5x + 4 = 0. What force did the crew log, in N?

A test sled of mass 32,000 g rides a factory rail and is driven with an acceleration whose value in m/s² equals the area under the curve y = 4x² + 7x between x = 0 and x = 2. The rail's data logger reports the driving force required for this in kN. The engineer then adds a 23 kN preload reading to that value. Next she subtracts 8 kN for a calibration offset and a further 10 kN for a brake correction. What is the engineer's final figure, in kN?

An electric go-kart's energy ledger over a 9-lap run is 9 times its single-lap balance. The single-lap balance is defined as the kart's energy of motion, expressed in kJ, minus the 14 kJ that its braking resistors absorb each lap, so it can be negative. The kart, of mass 60,000 g, reaches a speed in m/s equal to 10 times the larger solution of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. What is the 9-lap ledger value, in kJ?

A 17 kg drone test pod on an outdoor launch rail reaches a speed in m/s numerically equal to the area under the curve y = 2x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 4. Its energy of motion at that speed, less the 17 J lost to bearing friction during the run, is counted as the useful energy per run. The ambient wind speed along the rail was logged as 3.5 m/s. Two pods are launched per session and the crew runs 3 sessions, so the total useful energy is the per-run value multiplied by 2 and then by 3. Express that total in kJ.

The final figure in a warehouse conveyor report is expressed in kJ and represents the combined energy of motion of 10 identical crates riding the belt at the same time. The report obtains it by converting the combined energy from J to kJ. Each crate has a mass of 57 kg. The belt speed in m/s is twice the greatest common divisor of 57 and 252. What is the reported total, in kJ?

A workshop crane log records, in kN, the final total thrust produced by a pair of actuator sets working together. That total is twice the output of one set. Each set is itself made of 2 identical actuators, so a set's output is twice that of a single actuator. A single actuator accelerates a 49 kg counterweight at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 5x + 6 = 0. What total thrust does the log record, in kN?

The final entry in a tow-test log is a net force in kN, obtained by taking a measured pull, subtracting the 9 kN of resistance from the anchored chain, and then adding a 2 kN tailwind assist, with the direction of the pull taken as positive. The measured pull is the force needed to accelerate a 178 kg sled at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 9x + 14 = 0, converted to kN. The sled's tow rope was 15 m long. What net force appears in the log, in kN?

A 105 kg pallet on an automated warehouse shuttle is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 3x² + 3x between x = 2 and x = 3. The shuttle's drive must provide the force for this acceleration, less the 6 N that a passive roller contributes. The shuttle's track is 48 m long. The controller converts the drive force to kN and multiplies it by 12 to size the drive for a 12-shuttle system. What is the sized drive force, in kN?

The final value in a bridge-jack report is in kN and is found by adding 20 kN of dead-load allowance to a subtotal. That subtotal is 7 kN more than a net force expressed in kN. The net force is a jack's push minus 27 N of seal friction. The jack pushes a 123 kg beam with an acceleration in m/s² equal to the greatest common divisor of 120 and 55. The beam is 6.5 m long. What is the final value in the report, in kN?

A shipyard's final tally is a force in kN equal to 12 times a per-bay figure. The per-bay figure is 8 times a single-jack figure, which is expressed in kN. The single-jack figure is 30 N more than the force required to push a 134,000 g plate at an acceleration in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. The plate is 2.4 m wide. What is the shipyard's final tally, in kN?

The figure a race-team engineer finally quotes, in kJ, is 11 times a per-car figure. The per-car figure is the car's energy of motion plus 11 J of stored flywheel energy, converted to kJ. The car has a mass of 36,000 g. Its speed in m/s is 2 times the sum of 3 and 13. What figure does the engineer quote, in kJ?

A 31,000 g sled moves at a speed in m/s obtained by taking the area under y = 4x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 3 and subtracting 18. Its energy of motion is converted to kJ. The sled's brakes are rated to dump 23 kJ, and the log records the energy of motion minus that rating, which is negative when the brakes have spare capacity. The sled's track sits at an altitude of 450 m. What value does the log record, in kJ?

The value a lift engineer reports, in kN, is 10 times a single-cable figure. The single-cable figure is a net force expressed in kN. That net force is 29 N less than the force needed to accelerate a 182,000 g counterweight at a rate in m/s² equal to the greatest common divisor of 327 and 183. What value does the engineer report, in kN?
